legacyGameplayEvidence.note: The total V1 duration is recovered. Per-pose V1 exposure and frame-indexed contact were not stored.

authoredRootContract.note: The silhouette changes around a fixed gameplay root. Body-center travel is secondary evidence and must not be converted into root translation.

hitCountContract.rule: Frames 01-02 may gather cyan energy but must not show opponent contact, a hit burst, or a second strike.

frames.motionTruth: Wide low base, torso pitched forward, both feet grounded, coat and hair already carrying rearward lag.
frames.v2AuthoringConstraint: Preserve the low ready silhouette and forward intent; no contact VFX.

frames.motionTruth: Weight gathers over the support side while the lead hand and shoulders begin the rotational arc.
frames.v2AuthoringConstraint: Cyan energy may gather at the hand, but it must read as anticipation rather than an impact.

frames.motionTruth: The upper-body line extends while the hips load the kick; this is the final compressed pre-contact silhouette.
frames.v2AuthoringConstraint: Keep the hand reach and body coil, remove any contact-looking burst, and do not slow the transition into frame 03.

frames.motionTruth: The right leg extends horizontally into the single contact while the left leg supports the body and the guard counterbalances the line.
frames.v2AuthoringConstraint: Use the hash-approved high-resolution style checkpoint as the visual source; preserve contact silhouette, skin tone, costume, cyan/gold language, and dark neutral edge treatment.

frames.motionTruth: The V1 cell is byte-identical to frame 03, so V2 must preserve the intended impact exposure while resolving the duplicate-art gap with a distinct no-hit follow-through.
frames.v2AuthoringConstraint: Continue the same leg and hip momentum slightly past contact, begin recoil, and remove the impact spark. Do not create a second hit.

frames.motionTruth: The striking knee retracts, the torso rises, and coat/hair lag continues the completed kick arc.
frames.v2AuthoringConstraint: Preserve the raised-knee recoil and secondary lag; do not snap directly to neutral.

frames.motionTruth: Lamuh absorbs the rotation through a low settling shape while coat movement resolves toward the neutral recovery direction.
frames.v2AuthoringConstraint: Keep the low recovery silhouette long enough to read, then transition naturally to idle or walk without adding gameplay frames.

benchmarkQuestions: Does frame 00 expose intent without making Lamuh feel heavy?
Do frames 01-03 accelerate as one continuous body-driven arc?
Does frame 03 remain the only visible contact?
Does the duplicate contact exposure read as impact rather than dead time?
Do frames 05-06 carry momentum back into neutral without teleporting?
